Stop Doing This! 5 Habits That Can Ruin Your Home AC
Mar 31st, 2026
An air conditioner (AC) functions to cool down a room so it feels comfortable and refreshing. With a properly working AC, homeowners can stay relaxed indoors even when the weather outside is extremely hot. An AC is no longer considered a luxury, but a necessity for daily comfort.
Just like any other electronic appliance, an air conditioner requires regular maintenance. Proper care ensures that the unit functions efficiently, consumes energy wisely, and lasts for many years. Unfortunately, not all homeowners understand how to properly maintain their AC systems. Even if the unit comes with advanced features and a high price tag, it can still break down prematurely if it is not maintained correctly.
In addition to a lack of maintenance, certain everyday habits at home can also shorten the lifespan of your AC. Some of these habits may seem harmless, but over time they can lead to costly repairs or even total system failure.
So, what are these bad habits? Let’s take a closer look.
1. Rarely Cleaning the AC
Over time, dust, dirt, and debris naturally accumulate inside an air conditioner. When this happens, the unit cannot distribute cool air effectively throughout the room. As airflow becomes restricted, the system has to work harder to maintain the desired temperature.
When an AC is rarely cleaned, several problems may occur:
• Reduced cooling performance
• Higher electricity consumption
• Increased strain on internal components
• Poor indoor air quality
According to Mark Dawson, Chief Operating Officer of One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning, dirt and dust buildup inside the unit force components like the capacitor to work harder than they should. The harder the system works, the faster its parts wear out. When internal components operate under constant strain, the risk of overheating increases. Over time, this can damage critical parts such as the compressor, which is one of the most expensive components to replace.
To prevent this, homeowners should clean their AC units regularly. Most manufacturers recommend cleaning the unit every one to three months, depending on usage and environmental conditions. Additionally, air filters should be replaced or washed routinely. A clean filter allows air to circulate smoothly, improves cooling performance, and reduces energy consumption.
Neglecting basic cleaning may seem minor at first, but it is one of the most common reasons AC units fail prematurely.
2. Overusing the AC
During extremely hot weather, it is common for people to turn on their AC for long hours. However, some homeowners leave their AC running 24 hours a day to maintain constant cool temperatures.
While this may feel comfortable, continuous operation without breaks can significantly shorten the lifespan of the unit. When an AC runs non-stop for days, its internal components, especially the compressor, experience constant mechanical stress.
Over time, this can lead to:
• Faster wear and tear
• Overheating
• Higher electricity bills
• Reduced system efficiency
It is advisable to turn off the AC when the room is not in use or when leaving the house for extended periods. Allowing the system to rest helps prolong its operational life.
For those who are worried about forgetting to turn it off, modern air conditioners often come equipped with programmable timers. These timers allow users to schedule automatic shut-off after a certain number of hours.
Albert Lee, founder of Home Living Labs, explains that many modern AC systems can be programmed to turn on before homeowners return home. Some newer models can even be controlled via WiFi through a smartphone. These features provide convenience while preventing unnecessary overuse.
Using these smart features wisely can help maintain comfort without overburdening the system.
3. Placing the Outdoor Unit in a Confined or Hidden Area
A split AC system consists of two main components: the indoor unit and the outdoor unit. While many homeowners carefully choose the placement of the indoor unit for optimal cooling, they often overlook the importance of proper outdoor unit placement.
The outdoor unit is responsible for releasing heat extracted from inside the room. If it is placed in a narrow, enclosed, or poorly ventilated space, airflow becomes restricted. This prevents the system from effectively releasing heat, causing it to overheat.
Improper placement of the outdoor unit can lead to:
• Reduced cooling performance
• Increased energy consumption
• Overheating
• System shutdown or long-term damage
When the outdoor unit cannot expel heat efficiently, the entire system must work harder to compensate. This additional strain can significantly reduce the unit’s lifespan.
To avoid this problem, ensure that the outdoor unit is installed in a well-ventilated area with sufficient space around it. It should not be blocked by walls, furniture, or other objects that restrict airflow.
Proper installation is just as important as proper maintenance.
4. Installing the AC Near Heat Sources
Although an air conditioner is designed to cool a room, it should not be installed near appliances that generate heat.
Common household heat sources include:
• Refrigerators
• Televisions
• Ovens
• Stoves
• Direct sunlight from large windows
When an AC is placed near a heat source, it senses higher surrounding temperatures. As a result, the unit works harder and longer to cool the room. This constant effort increases energy consumption and accelerates wear on internal components. For example, installing an AC in a kitchen requires special consideration. The airflow direction should not blow directly toward a stove or cooking area, as the heat generated during cooking will force the system to overcompensate.
To maximize efficiency, install the indoor unit in a location where airflow can circulate evenly throughout the room without interference from heat-producing appliances. Proper placement helps the system maintain stable performance and prevents unnecessary stress.
5. Delaying Regular Servicing
One of the most common habits that causes AC systems to fail is delaying professional servicing. Many homeowners assume that as long as cool air is still blowing, the unit does not require maintenance. However, internal damage or wear may not always be visible or immediately noticeable. Small components inside the AC system may deteriorate gradually over time. According to AC technician Bradley Stroot, certain components, such as capacitors, may need replacement after several years of use, even if the system appears to be functioning normally. If these parts are not replaced in time, they can cause further damage to other components.
Ignoring minor issues can lead to:
• Major mechanical failure
• Expensive repairs
• Complete system breakdown
Preventive maintenance is far more affordable than emergency repairs. Scheduling professional servicing at least once or twice a year allows technicians to inspect, clean, and replace worn-out components before they cause significant damage. Routine servicing ensures that your AC continues to operate safely and efficiently.
Final Thoughts
Your air conditioner plays a crucial role in maintaining comfort inside your home, especially during hot weather. However, many common household habits can unintentionally shorten its lifespan.
To recap, avoid these five harmful habits:
1. Rarely cleaning the unit
2. Running the AC continuously without rest
3. Placing the outdoor unit in a confined area
4. Installing the AC near heat sources
5. Delaying regular servicing
By practicing proper maintenance, using smart features wisely, and ensuring correct installation, you can significantly extend the life of your air conditioner. Taking care of your AC not only saves money on repairs and electricity bills but also ensures consistent comfort for years to come.
A well-maintained air conditioner is not just an appliance, it is a long-term investment in your home’s comfort and efficiency.
